competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). regime.label: Constructive tape, but event and rate risk argue against chasing
regime.note: SPY gained 3.0% over the latest 20 settled sessions while the September 15–16 FOMC meeting is 12 tick-days away. Momentum leadership is narrow and several screen leaders are stretched: CRM rose 39.1% in 20 sessions with RSI(14) 80.8, while MRNA rose 151.7%. The portfolio therefore keeps 40% cash and uses small, catalyst-linked positions rather than buying the highest raw momentum scores.

analyst.thesis: What changed since the 2026-08-03 tick: the prior energy sleeve's event window has passed, and the positions mostly recovered—COP +10.4%, DVN +7.3%, CVX +5.4%, while FANG remained -0.6% versus entry. That made the trade profitable name-by-name, but it did not repair the portfolio process: the book is still -13.6% versus SPY +1.0% all-time (alpha -14.6 points) with a -4.02 annualized Sharpe. The catch-up therefore harvests the energy sleeve instead of inventing a new reason to keep an expired catalyst trade. VRTX becomes the anchor because Q2 revenue grew 12% to $3.33 billion, guidance rose to $13.1-$13.2 billion, the Crinetics acquisition is expected to close in Q3, and povetacicept has a November 30 PDUFA date. NEM adds a different factor: Q2 free cash flow was $2.2 billion, AISC was $1,621/oz, the Nevada Gold Mines disputes were resolved August 10, and Red Chris is progressing toward a second-half final investment decision. CRM gets only 12% despite strong Q2 results because the move already happened; the position is explicitly for the September 1 product-adoption webinar and September 16 Investor Day, with a limit to avoid paying through another gap. BAC is the rate-sensitive sleeve into the September 15-16 FOMC and has a September 4 ex-dividend date. The portfolio exits PYPL because its prior merger-floor narrative is no longer a sourced forward thesis, and exits LLY/FANG/COP/DVN/CVX because their named earnings/geopolitical catalysts have passed.

evidence.point: Vertex reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.33 billion, up 12%, raised full-year revenue guidance to $13.1-$13.2 billion, expects the Crinetics acquisition to close in Q3, and lists a November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date.
Robinhood fundamentals on 2026-08-31: VRTX P/E 31.514676, market cap $138.235 billion, and 52-week range $374.17-$555.69; settled 8/28 close $541.69.
Newmont reported Q2 free cash flow of $2.2 billion, 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, AISC of $1,621/oz, and reiterated 5.3 million ounce full-year production guidance.
Newmont and Barrick said their August 10 agreement resolves all outstanding Nevada Gold Mines disputes and contributes Fourmile, Fiberline, and Mike to the joint venture.

Salesforce Q2 FY27: revenue $11.3 billion (+11%), cRPO $33.5 billion (+14% constant currency), non-GAAP EPS $5.90 (+103%), operating cash flow $1.3 billion (+71%), and free cash flow $1.1 billion (+81%).
Salesforce scheduled a Q2 FY27 Product Adoption & Momentum webinar for September 1 and Investor Day for September 16, 2026.
The Federal Reserve's next scheduled FOMC meeting is September 15-16, 2026, with a Summary of Economic Projections.
Robinhood fundamentals on 2026-08-31: BAC P/E 14.342263, P/B 1.584070, 52-week range $46.115-$65.225, and September 4 ex-dividend date.
Randomized full-universe screen through 2026-08-28: VRTX +13.5%/20d with RSI 61.4; NEM +36.6% with RSI 64.5; CRM +39.1% with RSI 80.8; BAC +0.6% with RSI 50.8; SPY +3.0%.

risks: VRTX's Crinetics close is only guided to Q3, not a guaranteed date, and the November 30 PDUFA is roughly 65 tick-days away.
NEM already rose 36.6% in 20 sessions; a stronger dollar, higher real yields, or execution issues at Cadia/Red Chris can reverse the move.
CRM is the clearest chase risk: RSI(14) is 80.8 after a 39.1% 20-session gain. The 12% cap and buy limit are deliberate.
BAC is a macro expression, not a company-specific earnings trade; the September FOMC can flatten rather than steepen the curve.
Forty percent cash limits drawdown but will continue to create opportunity-cost alpha drag if the broad rally accelerates.

reflection.looking_back: The prior tick reduced the energy sleeve after a geopolitical shock but still carried DVN, COP, FANG, and CVX. By 2026-08-28, COP was +10.4%, DVN +7.3%, CVX +5.4%, and FANG -0.6% versus entry; VRTX led the non-energy holdings at +11.0%. Despite those winners, the book remained -13.6% versus SPY +1.0% all-time, for -14.6 points of alpha and a -4.02 annualized Sharpe.
worked: Reducing rather than abandoning the energy sleeve preserved upside in COP, DVN, and CVX while limiting FANG's lack of follow-through.
VRTX's thesis held: the position gained 11.0% versus entry and Q2 results raised full-year revenue guidance.
missed: The portfolio stayed too fragmented across eight names and too cash-heavy to repair alpha even when several calls worked.
PYPL had no durable dated catalyst; keeping it after the original floor thesis faded left a weakly grounded position that fell 6.2% over the latest 20 sessions.
reflection.adjustment: Harvest the expired energy-event sleeve, exit unsupported PYPL and post-event LLY, consolidate to four forward-catalyst names, and keep a deliberate—but smaller—40% cash reserve. New entries use ~1%-above-close limits to prevent gap chasing.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-08-28, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
